title: A 184.8dB-FoMs 1.6MS/s Incremental Noise-Shaping Pipeline ADC with Single-Amplification-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation Technique
problem: Incremental ADCs combining low-power SAR with high-resolution ΔΣ modulator suffer from slow conversion at high precision (kHz range); recent NS-SAR improves speed (300kS/s) but reduced oversampling ratio (OSR) causes sampling noise; kT/C noise cancellation requires static or repeatedly-triggered amplifiers, consuming power throughout entire conversion cycle.
motivation: IoT and sensor nodes demand high-accuracy low-power ADCs; incremental zoom architecture provides excellent SNR and integration, but slow conversion limits applicability. Concurrent coarse/fine quantization (dynamic zoom) shows promise but requires repeated sampling.
method: The converter combines coarse and fine quantization (precision measurement at two levels simultaneously) to digitize signals. It removes thermal noise in capacitors (kT/C noise) using an amplifier that operates only during the cancellation phase, not throughout conversion—drastically reducing power compared to designs that keep the amplifier always active. By processing both measurement levels concurrently and activating the amplifier only when needed, the design avoids repeated sampling overhead that slowed earlier incremental converters.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a gated amplifier (one that activates only during noise cancellation) enabling simultaneous coarse and fine measurements without repeated sampling.
contributions: 184.8dB FoM (figure of merit: 2^ENOB / (2 * conversion_time * power), excellent energy efficiency)
1.6MS/s conversion rate (5x faster than conventional zoom, competitive with NS-SAR)
High resolution via noise-shaping (exact bit resolution not in abstract, but FoM suggests 15+ bits)
Reduced power consumption via gated amplification
Concurrent coarse/fine conversion (simpler than sequential zoom, no repeated sampling)
